subject: DataCrest bake-off: post-demo synthesis and next-step plan
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@datacrest.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: DataCrest bake-off: post-demo synthesis and next-step plan

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for your time this morning. Quick synthesis from our side and proposed next steps so everyone is aligned.

Top pain points you called out
- Burstiness: unpredictable traffic spikes during batch reporting windows that blow out token costs.
- Latency tail: p95 latency spikes during peak that break your live annotator workflow.
- Data residency & controls: need customer-managed keys + audit logs for VOC and retention policy enforcement.
- Model quality parity: want feature parity with current hosted vendor (vendor A) on prompt fidelity and reranking.

Stated goals for the bake-off
- Confirm p95 generation latency <= 200ms for typical short prompts (<=128 tokens).
- Achieve cost target: average inference net cost < $0.85 per 1K tokens on steady-state.
- Prove secure deployment options: VPC + KMS + accessible audit trail.
- Maintain current quality: match or exceed vendor A on your sample eval set.

Decision criteria (proposed weights)
- Latency & availability: 35%
- Unit economics (per-token): 25%
- Security/compliance fit: 20%
- Integration effort & observability: 10%
- Model quality / regression risk: 10%

Open questions we committed to answer
- Full telemetry exposure (per-token breakdown + trace correlation): we will provide a sample trace export.
- KMS integration approach and sample key policies.
- Support for quantized model variants and fallback policies across capacity tiers.
- How prefix caching would interact with your annotator pipeline.

Proposed bake-off plan (4 weeks)
Week 0 (this week): kickoff & test matrix agreement (owner: DataCrest / Emily)
Week 1: baseline perf sweep vs your canonical prompt set (owner: Redwood infra)
Week 2: security & deployment validation (KMS, VPC, audit logs) + SOC2 evidence (owner: Redwood security)
Week 3: quality/regression evals + final summary (owner:双方)

Action items (owners & ETA)
- Emily: confirm the canonical prompt set + 3 priority user flows by Tue 2026-07-06
- Nikhil: share bake-off matrix & initial pricing quote (attached) — today
- Marissa: schedule technical kickoff with infra team and share availability — by Fri 2026-07-03
- Connor: prepare perf harness and test runners, include competitor baselines (OrbitAI & VertexAI) — by Mon 2026-07-06

Attachments: datacrest-bakeoff-matrix.xlsx (template), redwood-pricing-quote.pdf (initial estimate)

Links: HubSpot deal HC-2026-00456; Drive folder with demo assets (link below).

If this reads correct, Emily — can you confirm kickoff availability next Tuesday (2026-07-07) at 10am PT?

Thanks,
Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
nikhil.sharma@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0134

Nikhil — thanks for the clear write-up. This matches what we discussed. A few clarifications / asks from my side:

1) Timeline: 4 weeks sounds fine but we need a formal kickoff with procurement/legal in the first week. Procurement contact is procurement@datacrest.ai (cc'd on the next email).
2) Competitors: we will also include OrbitAI in the comparison (we already have a small sandbox there). We expect Redwood to run the same canonical prompts so results are apples-to-apples.
3) Data residency: we will need to validate that logs and audit trails can be retained in our AWS account / region — please confirm whether Redwood can push audit exports to a DataCrest S3 bucket.
4) Redaction: one of our flows needs PII redaction before logs are stored — can you confirm the supported redaction hooks/filters?

I can confirm the canonical prompt set by Mon 2026-07-06. Kickoff on Tue 2026-07-07 10am PT works for me.

Best,
Emily Zhao
Head of AI Integrations | DataCrest

Subject: Internal: DataCrest bake-off — owners & test plan

Team — quick internal note after Emily / procurement replies.

Summary: DataCrest is committed to a 4-week bake-off. Key asks: p95 latency targets, per-token cost target, KMS & audit exports, and PII redaction. They will include OrbitAI as a competitor; VertexAI is already in their sandbox.

Immediate tasks (I assigned):
- Marissa: own procurement lane — send redwood SOC2 (attached) & populate PIF; coordinate SLA/discount ask. Target: EOD Mon 2026-07-06.
- Connor: perf harness + competitor baselines (OrbitAI, VertexAI). Please ensure test runner records p50/p95/p99 and cost-per-1K token for each run. Target: test harness ready by Mon 2026-07-06.
- Me (Nikhil): draft kickoff agenda and bake-off rubric (weights above). I will own kickoff coordination with DataCrest and follow up on S3 audit export feasibility with infra/security.

Notes on competitive framing: rather than a pure head-to-head latency score, propose we run two buckets — (A) short interaction latency (<=128 tokens) and (B) long-context blackbox (>=1024 tokens) to surface any KV-cache/attention scaling differences. Call out fallback policies and quantized model variants in the report.

I'll attach the SOC2 and initial pricing in the reply to procurement. LMK if anything else.

Thanks,
Nikhil
